directAnswer: Pope Celestine IV was Goffredo da Castiglione of Milan, cardinal bishop of Sabina, who was elected in October 1241 after a harsh confinement of the cardinals in Rome and died about two weeks later, before he could be crowned.

paras: Goffredo came from Milan and served as a cardinal under Gregory IX, eventually as cardinal bishop of Sabina. When Gregory died in August 1241, Emperor Frederick II's forces were near Rome and two cardinals were his prisoners. The Roman senator Matteo Rosso Orsini locked the remaining cardinals in the ruined Septizodium on the Palatine to force a quick decision.

Conditions were severe in the summer heat, and the English cardinal Robert of Somercotes died during the confinement. This forced seclusion is often described as the first conclave in the strict sense. After weeks of deadlock the cardinals chose Goffredo on October 25, 1241.

sections.h2: Seventeen Days and a Long Vacancy
paras: Already elderly and apparently weakened by the ordeal, Celestine died on November 10, 1241, before his coronation. Almost no acts of his pontificate are recorded. Fearing a repeat of their confinement, many cardinals left Rome, and the Holy See remained vacant for about a year and a half, until the election of Innocent IV in June 1243. Little else is known about Celestine IV.

keyFacts: Personal name: Goffredo da Castiglione, of Milan
Elected in the Septizodium under pressure from senator Matteo Rosso Orsini
Died before his coronation; followed by a vacancy of about nineteen months

faqs.question: Why was Celestine IV's election so difficult?
faqs.answer: Frederick II held two cardinals captive, and the rest were confined by Roman authorities in the Septizodium under harsh conditions until they agreed, a process in which one cardinal died.

faqs.question: Was Celestine IV ever crowned?
faqs.answer: No. He died on November 10, 1241, about seventeen days after his election, before a coronation could take place.
